the linkages of accountability are empirically weak, and that this is true for all three linkages, in both presidential and parliamentary systems, in both majoritarian and proportional electoral systems, in both rich and poor countries, and in all major topical areas of research on electoral accountability.
the electoral accountability model is empirically valid, but that its validity is conditional on the existence of a second linkage in the chain of accountability.

electoral accountability is a weak force, but it is a force that can be strengthened through institutional reforms.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
electoral accountability is not the simple, direct, and linear process it is often portrayed to be.

we find that electoral accountability is a weak and conditional force, not a strong and pervasive one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the causal linkages in democratic accountability are more complex than is generally recognized.
electoral accountability is a more complex and less powerful process than many scholars have supposed.
the electoral accountability chain is more complex and more fragile than we have previously thought.
